name: ButtonFilter
intent: Filter chip for lists and tables: shows the filter name or its chosen value, opens its options, and turns an applied filter on or off.
usage: Use ButtonFilter for filter controls above tables and lists, like Status or Owner, and in the Toolbar filter bar. To open options, use DropdownMenu with trigger filter: it renders this button and opens the menu. Nothing set: one quiet outline with the chevron; the whole button opens the options. Once a filter is set (value or count) it turns blue; with onToggle it splits in two: the name turns the filter on or off (off keeps the selection, drawn dashed) and the chevron opens the options. hasDropdown false makes a plain on/off chip. See contracts/buttonfilter.json for the full contract.

size.note: Heights 28 / 36 / 44, same as Button. The chevron part is square. Without a size, a surrounding Density picks it: compact sm, default md, comfortable lg.

open.note: Dropdown is open. Sets aria-expanded and turns the chevron.

count.note: Applied values, like 3 statuses. Above 0 the filter is set and shows a Count.

value.note: The chosen value. Shows as Status: Pending, the name quieter than the value.

toggle.note: On or off once a filter is set. Leave it out and a set filter is on. Off keeps the selection but does not apply it: dashed outline, gray count.

onToggle.note: () => void. With a filter set, the name part becomes its own button that turns it on or off, and only the chevron opens the options.

hasDropdown.note: false: a plain on/off chip with no chevron, for filters with no value to pick. Clicking it calls onToggle.

onClick.note: Opens the options: the whole button when nothing is set, or the chevron once it splits. DropdownMenu trigger=filter wires this for you.

useWhen: Filters above a table or list, like Status, Owner or Date.
A filter the user can keep but switch off for a moment, without losing what they picked.
doNot: Do not invent a local split button, filter chip or dropdown trigger. Use DropdownMenu trigger=filter for the menu.
Do not use for page actions or view switches. Use Button or a DropdownMenu.
Do not put more than one word or two in the name.
Do not show the count as text in the label. Pass count.
a11y: Nothing set: one native button with aria-haspopup=menu and aria-expanded.
Split: the name is a toggle button with aria-pressed; the chevron is a separate button named Status options, with aria-haspopup and aria-expanded.
Its name is the filter name or Name: value, plus the count, like Status, 3 filters applied.
Each button has its own focus ring.
snippet: <DropdownMenu trigger="filter" label="Status" text={statusLabel} toggle={statusOn ? "on" : "off"} onToggle={toggleStatus} closeOnSelect={false} items={statusOptions} onSelect={pickStatus} />
